task.goal: Reduce mobile checkout LCP P75 from 4.2s to 2.5s or below on 4G without breaking checkout interaction or URL stability.
task.context: A React 16 application has 340 class components, webpack 4, a 2.8MB entry bundle (890KB gzip), three unused dependencies, an uncompressed 1.6MB hero image, and a four-weight Chinese font. Checkout routes must keep their current URLs and client-side navigation. The team has four engineers and two active feature commitments.

constraints.text: All existing checkout and marketing URLs must remain unchanged.
Checkout controls and client-side navigation must remain interactive; no delayed hydration that drops clicks.
The change must be safely deployable within two weeks without freezing other work.
No backend API contract changes are allowed.
The result must be measurable in real-user monitoring, not only a lab score.
Checkout visual layout should remain materially unchanged.

success.text: Mobile 4G LCP P75 is at or below 2.5 seconds in real-user monitoring.
Existing E2E tests remain green and client-side route transitions still occur.
Initial route JavaScript gzip size decreases by at least 40 percent.
No material increase in checkout conversion errors or CLS.

candidates.title: Remove unused dependencies and split routes
candidates.summary: Cut known dead weight and lazy-load non-checkout routes without changing route definitions.
candidates.mechanism: Remove unused moment and full lodash imports, dynamically import chart.js only on reporting pages, enable webpack splitChunks, and use route-level React.lazy for non-checkout screens while preserving existing paths.
assumptions: Static analysis has found no dynamic references to the removed dependencies
Checkout does not import reporting code indirectly
risks: A dynamic import boundary could alter loading order
A missed dynamic reference could fail a rarely used route
validation: Run bundle analyzer and gzip-size gate
Run full E2E including client-side navigation
Compare RUM LCP and checkout errors by cohort

candidates.title: Optimize LCP image and font delivery
candidates.summary: Reduce blocking image and font bytes while preserving responsive fallbacks.
candidates.mechanism: Generate AVIF/WebP and responsive srcset variants for the LCP image, preload only the selected source, subset the Chinese font to the actual glyph set, reduce unused weights, and preserve format fallbacks.
assumptions: The hero image is the LCP element for the target cohort
Two font weights are sufficient for checkout
risks: Wrong LCP attribution would make the optimization irrelevant
Font subsetting can create missing-glyph regressions
validation: Verify LCP element attribution in RUM
Run visual and glyph regression tests
Measure transfer bytes and CLS on low-end Android

candidates.title: Prerender a checkout shell
candidates.summary: Send a static shell early while preserving client-side checkout hydration.
candidates.mechanism: Add a route-specific prerendered shell containing stable layout and loading placeholders, then hydrate the existing checkout components as data arrives. Keep all existing URLs and API calls.
assumptions: The shell can be generated without user-specific data
Hydration boundaries can be introduced around class components
risks: Shell and hydrated DOM can diverge
Users may see placeholders too long on slow networks
validation: Run checkout interaction E2E under throttled 4G
Test rollback to the current renderer

candidates.title: Precache checkout assets with a service worker
candidates.summary: Make repeat checkout visits fast by caching the route bundle and fonts.
candidates.mechanism: Install a versioned service worker that precaches stable checkout assets after first load and uses stale-while-revalidate for static resources.
assumptions: The target cohort has repeat visits
Service-worker lifecycle can be introduced without stale checkout code
risks: Stale assets can create mixed-version checkout behavior
validation: Run first-visit and repeat-visit RUM separately

candidates.title: Move checkout rendering to edge SSR
candidates.summary: Replace the existing webpack rendering path with an edge-rendered application.
candidates.mechanism: Migrate checkout routes to a modern server-rendered framework with edge caching and streaming data, then preserve URLs through rewrites.
assumptions: The team can migrate class components without freezing parallel work
All checkout dependencies support the target runtime
validation: Run route parity and full E2E
Run edge failure and rollback drills

candidates.title: Delay hydration until idle
candidates.summary: Paint static HTML immediately and hydrate React after the browser is idle.
candidates.mechanism: Render a prerendered page and call hydration from requestIdleCallback after the first paint, with a fallback timeout.
assumptions: Users rarely interact during the initial idle window
risks: Clicks can be lost or ignored
The page can appear interactive while it is not
SEO and accessibility behavior can diverge
